..
Issued at 329 PM CDT Tue Aug 4 2026

Currently through this evening...

A swath of scattered showers and thunderstorms continue to make 
their way east across the forecast area today...a trend that 
will continue on through the rest of this afternoon. Looking 
aloft...upper air and satellite data showing generally zonal 
flow in place across the region. Across the CONUS, upper level 
low pressure is spinning in the GA/SC area, while the main area 
of high pressure centered over the Desert SW is being dampened 
by low pressure/broad troughing over much of central/western 
Canada into the northern CONUS. Satellite imagery shows 
shortwave disturbances embedded in the main overall flow...one 
of which is helping drive the ongoing activity across the 
forecast area. At the surface, the forecast sits just north of 
the main cold front...which has stalled some, currently sitting 
from SW/south central KS up into ESErn IA. Behind this frontal 
boundary, winds have been gusty (esp. by August standards) out 
of the NNE...gusts have mainly been around 25-30 MPH. Between 
the plentiful cloud cover, scattered precipitation and sitting 
on the north side of the frontal boundary...not surprising that 
in spots temperatures have been struggling so far today. By the 
time it's all said and done...forecast highs across southern 
areas will turn out alright...but some spots across south 
central NE may not end up even hitting 70 degrees. Still some 
time to recover behind this activity anywhere there are breaks 
in the cloud cover. 
 
For the rest of today...main concern lies with the ongoing
activity. There have been spots at times that have perked up 
in strength...but the overall environment is not supportive of a
notable severe weather threat. Not out of the question that 
some storms could be strong...with gusty winds/small hail the 
main threats. Instability is sitting around 500-1000 j/kg across
central/NErn areas, closer to 1500 j/kg in the SE...but both 
low and mid level lapse rates are pretty low. Timing of the main
swath has it clearing the forecast area early this 
evening...and while there could be some isolated lingering 
activity, models showing a relative lull...with better lift 
along an increasing LLJ looking to focus just off to our east.

Later tonight through Wednesday...

Mainly after midnight tonight, models showing another embedded 
weaker shortwave disturbance making its way out of the Rockies 
and onto the Plains...ushering the next chance for 
showers/thunderstorms. Higher-res models aren't in too bad of 
agreement showing that as far as timing goes...the better 
chances hold off until closer to/after 09Z. Little more 
uncertainty with the overall coverage initially, so PoPs remain 
broad with chances in place CWA-wide. The overall best chances 
run roughly from around sunrise through the early afternoon 
hours...dropping off from west to east, possibly dry area-wide 
by mid-afternoon. The highest chances remain focused through the
heart of the forecast area, roughly from I-80 to near the state
line...though at least 20-30 percent chances are outside that 
corridor to cover the rest of the area. Not anticipating this 
activity to be severe...with the SPC Day 2 outlook remaining 
well outside our boundaries. 

At the surface, winds won't be as gusty as they have been
today...as high pressure slides through the area. Winds turn 
more easterly with time, speeds topping out around 10 MPH. The 
daytime precipitation chances and lingering cloud cover make for
a tricky temperature forecast...as there will be some 
opportunity to recover if precip does in fact clear out by mid-
afternoon and we can get breaks in the cloud cover. Forecast 
highs through the central portions of the area are in the lower 
70s, with mid-70s to the north and south. 

Thursday and on...

Looking toward the end of this week on into the start of next 
week...overall there hasn't been any notable changes in the  
forecast. Big picture-wise...models continue to show the upper
level pattern through this timeframe flexing to varying 
degrees of west-northwest flow. The main area of upper level 
high pressure remains centered generally over the Desert SW...at
times able to amplify a bit more early-on thanks to deeper 
troughing over portions of the eastern CONUS...but then is 
dampened by additional activity moving onto western Canada/far 
NNWrn CONUS. Spotty, generally low-end preciptiation chances 
remain in the forecast...as there is still the potential for 
periodic shortwave disturbances to push through the region...but
confidence in the timing and tracking of any of these 
disturbances is pretty low at this point. 

Forecast continues to show a warming trend from the 70s of 
Wednesday...with low-mid 80s on Thursday increasing into the 90s-
near 100 for this weekend/Monday. Heat index values around 100-105 
are not out of the question Sat-Mon, especially for the southern 
half of the forecast area.
